subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
outcomes: I can name hair and face words: curly, straight, dark, fair, a beard, a moustache.
I can describe people in the right word order: She's got long, dark, curly hair.
I can write short sentences about how my family members look.

tf.s: The opposite of curly hair is straight hair.
tf.why: Yes! Curly and straight are opposites.

tf.s: In the poem, Dad has got a beard.
tf.why: Right! Dad is the one with a beard.

tf.s: We say "She's got curly, dark, long hair."
tf.why: Say long or short first: She's got long, dark, curly hair.

tf.s: A moustache grows above the mouth.
tf.why: Yes! A moustache is hair above the mouth.

tf.s: Fair hair is very dark hair.
tf.why: Fair hair is light in colour, the opposite of dark.

tf.s: In the poem, Laith has got a moustache.
tf.why: Yes! Laith has got a moustache and fair hair.

tf.s: In the poem, Thuriya has got short, straight hair.
tf.why: Thuriya has got long, dark, curly hair.

tf.s: We say "He's got a beard." to describe a man's face.
Tall and long are words for hair colour.
tf.why: Dark and fair are colours; long and short tell us how long hair is.

tf.s: "She's got long hair" and "She has got long hair" mean different things.
tf.why: She's got is the short form of she has got.

boxes.q: Who has got a beard in the poem?
boxes.why: In the poem, Dad has got a beard.

boxes.q: The opposite of long hair is ___ hair.
The opposite of dark hair is ___ hair.
boxes.why: Dark and fair are opposites for hair colour.
Long or short comes first, then colour, then curly or straight.
We say a beard and a moustache.

boxes.q: Hair that is not curly is ___.
boxes.why: Straight is the opposite of curly.

boxes.q: Which word is about hair colour?
boxes.why: Fair and dark tell us the colour of hair.
She has got, or she's got.

boxes.q: Which word describes a whole person, not hair?
Who is very tall with long, dark, curly hair?
boxes.why: The poem describes Thuriya like this.

hunt.q: In the poem, Laith's hair is ___.

mcq.q: Which list has only appearance words for hair?
mcq.why: Curly, straight, fair and dark describe hair.

mcq.q: What does Laith look like in the poem?
o: He's got a moustache and fair hair.
He's got a beard and dark hair.
He's very tall with curly hair.
mcq.why: The poem says Laith has got a moustache and his hair is fair.

mcq.q: What is the word order tip in this lesson?
mcq.why: We say long or short first: long, dark, curly hair.

mcq.q: What is the name of the poem in this lesson?
mcq.why: The poem is called My family's unusual.

mcq.q: Put the words in order: hair / curly / long / dark. She's got …
mcq.why: Long first, then colour, then curly.

mcq.q: Your brother is very tall. His hair is short, dark and curly. Which sentence is correct?
o: He's very tall. He's got short, dark, curly hair.
He's very tall. He's got curly, dark, short hair.
He's very short. He's got long, fair hair.
He's got very tall, dark, curly hair.
mcq.why: Short comes first, then dark, then curly.

mcq.q: Which sentence describes a man with hair on his chin?
mcq.why: Hair on the chin is a beard.

mcq.q: Which description is NOT correct English?
o: She's got curly, long, fair hair.
She's got long, fair, curly hair.
mcq.why: Long must come first, before fair and curly.

mcq.q: Your friend says: "She's got long, dark hair." Which picture matches?
o: a girl with long, dark hair
a girl with short, fair hair
a girl with short, dark hair
mcq.why: Long and dark must both be true.

mcq.q: Why is "curly hair – straight hair" a good pair to learn together?
mcq.why: Learning opposites together helps us remember both words.
